stories.title: Record Subsurface Warming In Monterey Bay: MBARI logs 18.18°C at 60m; tropical species move north

These shifts in ocean conditions pose a risk to deep-sea food availability, impacting various marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Bangka Slow Loris Rediscovered: Rescues reveal more than 90 venomous primates; habitat loss still threatens

Wildlife rescues have been instrumental not only in recording their existence but also in aiding rehabilitation efforts.

This programme has provided financial assistance to over 5,500 families facing housing insecurity in the Atlanta area. By streamlining processes and collaborating with landlords, the programme aims to prevent evictions and court backlogs. Follow-up surveys indicate that a majority of recipients remain in stable housing a year later.

stories.title: Louisiana woman wins nearly $450,000 after $32,500 river barrier fails and home shifts

stories.title: Howard Stern's wife Beth turns grief into rescue mission, helping over 2,000 cats find homes

This center improves the conditions for cats waiting for adoption and boosts rescue capabilities. With over 2,000 cats fostered since 2013, Beth's dedicated efforts have played a crucial role in spotlighting the importance of adopting shelter animals nationwide.

stories.title: Farm Becomes Wildlife Retreat: Olivia Newton-John reshaped Dalwood estate; sale tied to cancer work

Despite her husband's assets exceeding $1 million compared with her $39,000, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld the agreement, rejecting her claims of pressure and language difficulties.

stories.title: Meet Emily Herra, 17-year-old who turned a trash-filled lot into a community garden; won $10,000 for climate work
stories.summary: Co-founder of Veggie Nuggets, Emily Herra, collaborated with a team to revitalize an abandoned plot into a vibrant community garden. Despite facing setbacks, such as a contractor's destruction of their work, the group demonstrated resilience and rebuilt their garden. Their dedication earned them the Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes, which aids future climate activism. Herra's initiative spotlights the impactful role youth can play in fostering sustainability in their communities.

stories.title: 'Rahul camp insecure of Priyanka': BJP alleges rift between siblings, accuses leader of opposition of 'sidelining' sister
Lady Gaga and her mother built youth mental-health foundation; its programme has now crossed 100,000 certificates worldwide
stories.summary: Lady Gaga and her mother, Cynthia Germanotta, celebrated a remarkable achievement with the Born This Way Foundation as they announced that more than 100,000 individuals have successfully earned the Be There Certificate worldwide. This milestone, part of the Generation Be There campaign, emphasizes the foundation's commitment to promoting mental health awareness and education, enabling compassionate responses to those facing mental health challenges in their communities.

stories.title: Utah businessman mailed thousands of bricks, forcing the US to rewrite postal rules
Ayodhya Ram temple donation embezzlement case: Chargesheet filed, Supreme Court allows petitioners to assist trial
'Act responsibly': Taliban urges US over planned deportation of Afghan immigrants
California teen wins $10,000 for system that controls computers using tongue movements and blinks
stories.summary: Hollie Tang, a talented student from Wilson High School, has innovatively developed a system named Tonguage, designed to empower individuals with disabilities. This groundbreaking technology enables users to navigate devices through tongue movements and eye blinks. Winning the top scholarship at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair in Phoenix, Tang highlighted the potential of technology to enhance lives.

stories.title: Meet the three former AAP leaders who switched sides to join BJP ahead of Punjab polls
'Don't take court for granted': Delhi court summons actor Nora Fatehi again in Rs 200-crore extortion case
‘Youth-oppressive NDA govt’: Tejashwi accuses Nitish of toppling Mahagathbandhan regime in 2024
Big setback for AAP ahead of Punjab elections; 3 rebel MLAs join BJP
2 Congress workers held for hurling beer bottles at BJP headquarters in Kerala
stories.summary: In a heated political climate in Thiruvananthapuram, two Congress party workers were apprehended for allegedly hurling beer bottles at the BJP headquarters in Kerala. The situation escalated tensions between the rival parties. Following protests and demands from BJP for arrests, the police utilized CCTV footage for a thorough investigation, leading to the identification of the suspects as local Congress members involved in the incident.

stories.title: Punjab: AAP to seek cancellation of membership of 2 MLAs after they quit party
'2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
stories.summary: In a momentous gathering, the INDIA bloc's supporters came together at Ramlila Maidan to address pressing political issues. Leaders from multiple parties spoke passionately about the necessity for change, particularly calling for the ousting of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This event highlighted the importance of unity against perceived electoral injustices, with speakers weaving in historical contexts to bolster their arguments regarding voting rights and electoral fairness.

stories.title: Kiren Rijiju jibes at Congress over INDIA bloc's Ramlila rally crowd photo, calls it 'AI-generated'
J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
Fresh Iran strikes after US midterms? Inside Trump-Netanyahu's 'tough' call
stories.summary: Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a tough phone call regarding Iran and military strategies. They discussed the possibility of military action after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump expressed readiness for diplomacy, while Netanyahu urged immediate strikes against Iran. Diplomatic initiatives continue, with the US Vice President sending a letter to Iran's national security chief.

stories.title: Desi Bullet Train closer to reality as squeeze test nears completion
6 Indian trekkers 'ignore weather warnings', get stranded in Nepal
SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
Could Einstein’s equations explain the universe’s expansion?
stories.summary: Researchers from UC Davis have proposed that dark energy may not be necessary to explain the universe's acceleration. They found weak points in the Lambda-cold dark matter model using Einstein's equations. By examining instabilities in Friedmann spacetimes, they suggest alternative explanations for cosmic expansion. Their work raises questions about the Copernican principle in the context of current models. This research could lead to significant shifts in our understanding of cosmology.

stories.title: Scientists have developed a new technology that could make electric car batteries smaller, lighter and longer-lasting, potentially letting drivers travel farther on a single charge without carrying a heavier battery
stories.summary: Scientists from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology developed a new technology for anode-free batteries. This innovative approach focuses on enhancing lithium deposition to improve battery efficiency and longevity. By restructuring the copper surface for lithium storage, they have addressed issues with dendrite formation. Applying a thin layer of MXene further stabilizes the battery's performance.

stories.title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
Ranch Easement Preserves Habitat: Winn descendants shield 165 acres; Blanco River recharge gains
stories.summary: Four Winns Ranch in Texas, a treasured historical site, is preserved through dedicated efforts by the Winn family alongside conservation partners. Spanning 165 acres, this land is vital for protecting local wildlife habitats and water sources. Originally acquired by the noteworthy artist James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., the ranch possesses rich cultural heritage while fostering agricultural and ecotourism activities, aiding the survival of rare birds and endangered aquatic species.

stories.title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
12th century Nepalese Manjushri statue sold for about Rs 166 crore in 2026
stories.summary: A 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal recently sold for around ₹166 crore, illuminating the exceptional artistry of Newar creators from the Kathmandu Valley. This sculpture's intriguing journey through different collections illustrates its cultural significance and uniqueness. Furthermore, the influence of Newar craftsmanship on Buddhist art permeated throughout Tibet and Asia, showcasing Nepal's profound artistic legacy and its vital role in international art history.

stories.title: 1984 survivors, Sikh groups question timing of INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, seek apology
Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
12-year-old London boy raises £13,000 for wildlife, wins Attenborough's praise

A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear deliberately aimed at his heart, scientists say, offering rare evidence of targeted violence among our closest ancient relatives
stories.summary: A recent archaeological find in Shanidar Cave revealed a Neanderthal skeleton showing signs of lethal violence, potentially from a wooden spear, suggesting that early human emotional responses might mirror those of today. The evidence hints at both a targeted attack and social care, as the skeleton bore previous injuries. This discovery serves as a window into the dualities of early human life, showcasing their capacity for both violence and compassion.

stories.title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
Golden Triangle's North East drug trade thrives on barter
£5 ivory chess piece found in family drawer sells for £735,000 after 55 years
stories.summary: An extraordinary Lewis chessman carving has fetched an impressive £735,000 at auction. Hidden away in a drawer for more than 55 years by the family of the dealer, this remarkable figure was revealed as a warder, part of the legendary Lewis Chessmen collection. Originally found in 1831, this collection comprises 93 intricately carved pieces from 1150 to 1200 AD, though the auction leaves four original pieces still unaccounted for.

stories.title: 82-year-old Florida man’s 70-year collection includes a letter from Elizabeth Taylor
In 1913, an Ohio couple sent their eight-month-old son to his grandmother through the postal service
stories.summary: In the year 1913, the US Postal Service unveiled Parcel Post, permitting the mailing of bigger packages. Ingenious parents even started shipping their small children to reduce travel expenses, gaining notoriety when six-year-old May Pierstorff was dispatched 73 miles away. This phenomenon sparked national debate, leading to the ban of child parceling, although similar incidents lingered until 1915, prompting stricter postal regulations to curb such extraordinary practices.

stories.title: Idaho Supreme Court revives condo owners' challenge to property changes approved by 88% vote
stories.summary: The Idaho Supreme Court has revived a legal dispute involving condominium owners challenging changes to property ownership. The contentious amendments were made by the Crystal Beach Condominium Association, affecting owners' shares and rental rules. A previous dismissal by a lower court has been partly overturned, confirming owners' rights to challenge changes impacting their property. Plaintiffs now have their claims for declaratory relief and title slander allowed to proceed.

stories.title: Texas court reopens insurance dispute after landslide destroys two homeowners' backyards
stories.summary: A legal dispute involving home insurance coverage in Travis County has been returned to court for further hearings. The Texas Third Court of Appeal overturned a previous ruling that held the insurer liable for damages. Homeowners claimed that earth movement caused significant damage to their properties, leading to a denial of their insurance claims. The appeals court requires the insurer to demonstrate the cause of the landslide.

stories.title: Florida has allocated $3 million to acquire a 642-acre property along the Suwannee River; officials say ending its current land use could save 159,000 gallons of water daily and reduce nutrient inputs
stories.summary: Florida has allocated $3 million for the acquisition of property along the Suwannee River to reduce water consumption. The Suwannee Sandhill Tract-Drew Property will help conserve approximately 158,800 gallons of water daily. This initiative is part of a larger $100 million investment aimed at various water conservation projects. The acquisition will facilitate the restoration of the land for wildlife habitats and public recreation.

stories.title: Dorothy Dandridge Home Listed: Former Hollywood Hills residence hits $5.499 million; price up nearly 90% from 2014 sale
stories.summary: A stunning Mediterranean-style home in Hollywood Hills, once owned by the iconic actress Dorothy Dandridge, is now on the market for nearly $5.5 million. Covering 4,368 square feet, the residence boasts four luxurious bedrooms and five opulent bathrooms. Dandridge's impactful legacy as a pioneering Black actress echoes through this property, complemented by breathtaking views of Los Angeles. The current owners have thoughtfully renovated it while respecting its historic charm.

stories.title: 'They'll become garbage': Trump says he'll become 'Mr. Veto' if Democrats win midterms
Poland’s top court turns into battleground as Tusk and pro-Trump president clash
Three held over pro-Khalistan graffiti at Delhi Metro stations after Diljit concert
Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
stories.summary: In a heartfelt gesture symbolizing the deep-rooted friendship between Bhutan and India, King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck dedicated a stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This event took place in Gelephu Mindfulness City, where 108 stupas are being raised. Union minister Kiren Rijiju represented India, conveying PM Modi's gratitude. The stupa, numbered 76, represents the strong ties shared by the two nations.

stories.title: CM Mann says opposition parties have nothing to offer Punjab, eyes AAP's return to power in 2027
California doctor Violetta Mailyan gets 15 years for $45 million Medicare fraud and fake Botox claims
stories.summary: California doctor Violetta Mailyan has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for defrauding Medicare of more than $45 million through fake Botox injection claims. Prosecutors said she used the money to buy five properties, two Tesla vehicles, including a Cybertruck, and expensive collectibles. She must also pay $32.9 million in restitution.

stories.title: 'Rahul trying to sideline Priyanka': BJP's big attack after INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally
UK Labour minister under fire for claiming employers are not ‘working people’
Coal India records highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 MT in Oct, up 19%
Beavers set to return to Loch Ness after 500 years, with 15 family groups approved for release.
stories.summary: In an exciting development, wild beavers are about to return to Loch Ness after centuries of absence. The Scottish nature agency NatureScot has sanctioned their release as part of a transformative rewilding project. Over the next three years, conservationists will introduce family groups of beavers to the area’s waterways, focusing on enhancing biodiversity and wildlife habitats, while also implementing strategies to resolve any conflicts with local farmers and landowners.

stories.title: Delaware couple wins disputed backyard land after 20 years, despite neighbours' $30,000 demand
stories.summary: After two decades of contention, a Delaware court officially awarded Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray ownership of a long-disputed parcel of land. The case arose when the Preradovic family challenged property lines after purchasing an adjacent lot. Failed negotiations led to litigation, ultimately resulting in the court granting the Murrays the rear yard while their claims to the front areas were rejected.

New airfare rules from next year: No govt intervention except in ‘extraordinary situations’ to prevent spikes
US: Multiple shootings on Halloween leaves 4 dead, 15 injured
‘Nobody can touch this Kumaraswamy’: Union minister dares cops, Karnataka govt over sting row
Florence Pugh's parents put £1.65 million Oxfordshire barn where the Oppenheimer star grew up on sale
stories.summary: Florence Pugh's parents, Clinton Pugh and Deborah Mackin, have listed their Grade II-listed Oxfordshire barn for £1.65 million. The Oppenheimer actress grew up in the 17th-century property, which her parents purchased for £950,000 in 2011. The couple are reportedly considering downsizing as their children have gradually moved out of the family home.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine struck Russian defence facility in Rostov
He was homeless twice, now he is a billionaire
stories.summary: John Paul DeJoria overcame homelessness not once, but twice, before establishing thriving ventures in the hair-care and spirits sectors. A dedicated philanthropist, he signed the Giving Pledge to relinquish a minimum of half his fortune. Through the JP’s Peace, Love & Happiness Foundation, he champions diverse initiatives, especially food security. Notably, the Grow Appalachia program has empowered countless families to cultivate their own food.

stories.title: Ming royal descendant turned Buddhist monk painted 12 leaves of birds and flowers, sold for Rs 75 cr
stories.summary: Bada Shanren, originally named Zhu Da, was born into the Ming royal lineage in 1626. Following the Ming dynasty's collapse in 1644, he sought solace in a Buddhist monastery for many years. Later, he embraced secular life as a renowned painter, crafting works that emphasize bold simplicity. His masterpiece, 'Flowers and Birds,' comprised twelve ink-on-paper leaves and recently fetched HK$61.9 million at Christie's Hong Kong auction.

stories.title: Dhak beats on the Thames! British Bengalis take Durga Puja to London's iconic river
stories.summary: British Bengalis marked the fifth annual Durga Parade on the River Thames in London this Saturday. The event featured a decorated idol of Goddess Durga sailing past famous landmarks like Big Ben and the London Eye. Musical performances and dancing were part of the celebrations aboard the boat, showcasing local talent. Bihar Tourism Minister Kedar Prasad Gupta attended and invited Indians to visit Bihar.

stories.title: Former Mossad officer helped Flávio Bolsonaro flee Brazil: Report
International Digi Yatra trials to begin at 7 airports for Indian nationals this year for wider rollout in 2027: Government
US girl starts selling slime to pay for school trip, gets 8 million views in a month
stories.summary: A 14-year-old Indiana girl who started selling slime and squishy toys to fund a school trip to Washington, DC, has attracted over eight million online views. Lexi Long launched her business, Slime & Squish, on October 1 and reached her fundraising goal within nine days. Her business has since gained more than 30,000 social media followers and attracted customers at local events and shops.

stories.title: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch opposes formal British apology for slave trade, calls it a 'navel-gazing distraction'
Pakistan gas crisis: Families return to firewood as LPG prices soar ahead of winter
Pippa Middleton and James Matthews ordered to remove an unauthorised car park at £15.5 million estate
stories.summary: Pippa Middleton, Princess Catherine’s sister, and her husband James Matthews have been ordered to demolish an unauthorised car park at their £15.5 million Barton Court estate. West Berkshire Council ruled against the development after local residents objected to construction without consultation, citing concerns over its impact on the rural character of Kintbury.

stories.title: CBI extradites Mahadev App kingpin Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman
'Vote chori, yes papa': Mamata takes 'Johny Johny' jibe at CEC Gyanesh - video

A Chester Zoo collection of Dracula orchids has been declared nationally important, drawing attention to rare flowers with bizarre, vampire-like appearances that are increasingly threatened in the wild.
stories.summary: Chester Zoo recently received National Plant Collection status for its impressive collection of Dracula orchids. These unique flowers, which mimic various shapes, face threats from habitat loss and illegal collection. Pollination occurs through specific fungi-attracting smells rather than traditional scents. Chester Zoo's horticulturists are dedicated to preserving these rare species amidst growing environmental challenges. Currently, the orchids are not on public display but contribute to plant biodiversity conservation efforts.

stories.title: Florida is planning 4,800 acres of wetlands at the mouth of the Kissimmee River to remove phosphorus before it reaches Lake Okeechobee, decades after engineers began undoing the river's earlier straightening
stories.summary: Florida is planning a 4,800-acre wetland project to filter phosphorus pollution before it reaches Lake Okeechobee. This initiative involves directing stormwater through treatment areas filled with aquatic vegetation. Wetlands help mitigate impacts of excess nutrients and support local ecosystems. The project has been under development since 2019 and will provide flood protection and recreational opportunities. A public meeting is scheduled for November 2026 to discuss construction details.

stories.title: A cupboard buried when Mount Vesuvius destroyed Pompeii in AD 79 has yielded 38 bronze coins and at least 24 tiny childhood charms; archaeologists say the objects reveal glimpses of a family's lost everyday life
stories.summary: Italian archaeologists recently uncovered a sealed wooden cupboard in Pompeii, revealing artifacts from 2,000 years ago. Among the findings were 38 bronze coins, personal care items, and a unique childhood necklace. The discovery adds to our understanding of daily life in ancient Rome, highlighting ordinary people's lives. It is speculated that the residents could not retrieve their belongings during the volcanic eruption.

stories.title: No paneer, no honey, no milky chai? The real challenge of going vegan in India
Trump says Bolsonaro can remain in US indefinitely, calls Brazil election a 'disgrace'
stories.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after his electoral defeat, despite having led in several opinion polls. His departure came after a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered his passport revoked. He is also facing two federal money-laundering investigations, while police in Brazil had considered him a flight risk. The comments came as US secretary of state Marco Rubio held talks with Brazilian foreign minister Mauro Vieira.

stories.title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has discussed the protection of civilian shipping with Russia, Ukraine, and European nations. Efforts are being made to restore grain exports through the Black Sea, which have significantly declined. Additionally, the safety of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments is a major concern amid the ongoing conflict. Different interpretations of energy infrastructure complicate discussions on protection measures.

stories.title: Joint List offers to back anti-Netanyahu government: Report
'Super flop rally': BJP says Ramlila Maidan '40% empty', mocks INDIA bloc protest
US midterms: Trump ready with plan to outmaneuver Democrat-controlled Congress
stories.summary: Senior aides, including deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller and budget director Russell Vought, have been working with the White House Counsel's Office since April to identify measures Trump could pursue without congressional approval. These include policies on immigration, tariffs, housing costs and federal spending, according to a White House official and two people familiar with the plans.

stories.title: Veiled marble bust sells for record €1.925 million in Vienna
stories.summary: A marble sculpture of a veiled lady created by Antonio Corradini recently sold for €1.925 million. The auction took place in Vienna and set a new world record for the artist. The sculpture is 60 centimeters tall and showcases intricate craftsmanship that mimics the look of cloth. Bidders from the saleroom and via telephone competed for the artwork, but a telephone bidder ultimately won.

stories.title: Florida court overturns order against couple accused of disrupting weddings at a historic mansion
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a Florida appeals court has reversed a previous order aimed at curbing a couple's disruptive activities that allegedly disrupted outdoor wedding ceremonies with loud machinery and gunfire. While the immediate limitations have been lifted, the legal battle persists with potential civil nuisance claims still on the table. The appeals court mandates that any new restrictions must strictly adhere to specific evidence criteria.

stories.title: Maya Jama donates £83,500 to charity after losing Celebrity Traitors, matching her potential prize money
stories.summary: Maya Jama, who participated in Celebrity Traitors, donated her potential prize of £83,500 to Action for Children. This charity supports children facing various hardships across the UK, including poverty and abuse. Following her exit in the show's finale, Jama shared her donation on social media platforms. Fellow contestants Sebastian Croft and Romesh Ranganathan each contributed their winnings to different charitable organizations.

stories.title: Rahul's Ramlila 'jalsa' to 'rub salt in wounds' of 1984 Sikh riot victims: Amit Shah
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah said the "jalsa" would reopen painful memories for the victims and their families, accusing the Congress of showing little sensitivity towards the tragedy. Shah made the remarks in Chandigarh while addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for development projects worth Rs 258 crore.

stories.title: 'Stay quiet or I'll speak for an hour': Kharge's playful warning to supporters at Ramlila Maidan rally
'After Gyanesh, you are next': Rahul Gandhi says PM Modi, Amit Shah will face justice for 'vote chori'
'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?': Mamata mocks CEC; Akhilesh invokes Haldighati - who said what at INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: During a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, senior leaders from the INDIA coalition raised alarms about electoral roll manipulation. They accused the BJP of endangering democracy through the Chief Election Commissioner. Opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee demanded Gyanesh Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.

stories.title: Inside UK PM’s Diwali party at his residence; Gita chanting to vegetarian snacks, woman shares
stories.summary: Shanu had the unique opportunity to celebrate Diwali at 10 Downing Street, the iconic residence of the UK Prime Minister. The event was beautifully adorned with traditional decorations, offering a range of vegetarian delicacies. During the gathering, the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his wife participated in lighting a ceremonial diya, emphasizing the importance of community contributions and the strengthening of UK-India relations.

stories.title: US couple's fence extends nine feet into neighbour's land, court rules in their favour
stories.summary: A Delaware couple who maintained a fence and garden for more than 20 years won a property dispute after their new neighbours demanded $30,000 to let them keep the land. The neighbours claimed the fence crossed the legal boundary, but an October 30 court ruling recognised the couple's ownership of the entire disputed strip, including an unfenced garden planter, through adverse possession.

stories.title: Safari West's 400-acre wildlife preserve enters a new nonprofit era after decades of conservation
‘Will dig you out from ground, if needed’: Kharge warns CEC Gyanesh Kumar at INDIA bloc rally
‘Did they really have to choose this day?’ BJP targets Congress over INDIA bloc rally on anniversary of 1984 riots
stories.summary: BJP organized a protest march in West Delhi's Hari Nagar demanding an apology from Congress for the 1984 anti-Sikh violence. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri described the killings as a well-planned genocide rather than a riot. Several leaders participated in the march, expressing concerns over Congress's perceived failure to acknowledge the tragedy. The protest coincided with the opposition's rally addressing electoral irregularities on the same day.

stories.title: ‘Deeply shameful’: Tharoor slams UK over colonialism omission in slavery apology
stories.summary: Responding to British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's remarks in a post on X on Saturday, Shashi Tharoor said he had long maintained that putting a monetary figure on the damage caused by British rule was difficult. He also said Britain had never formally apologised for the destruction and exploitation carried out during its colonial rule.

stories.title: DGCA mandates twin pilot operations from Monday, chopper operators threaten to suspend Char Dam flights
'Why do you challenge democracy?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of acting on behest of foreign powers
stories.summary: BJP leader Nitin Nabin accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of furthering foreign agendas at a rally in Haryana. Nabin criticized Congress for claiming democracy is at risk only when it loses elections in multiple states. He challenged allegations regarding voter deletion and past election irregularities linked to the party’s leadership. Nabin emphasized the need for governance based on the Constitution rather than dynastic politics.

stories.title: 'Every single shop forcibly shut': Rahul Gandhi targets BJP over Connaught Place closures during mega rally
'Cutting 130m voters unacceptable': Shashi Tharoor targets EC amid INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally
'Gyanesh Kumar can no longer remain in his position': TMC's Sagarika Ghose demands CEC's removal
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose has intensified calls for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down. Uniting the opposition for a common cause, leaders stress the urgency to restore trust in the electoral process. At a rally in Delhi, they highlighted the importance of safeguarding voting rights against authoritarian measures.

stories.title: US river straightened 110 years ago to drain land, now set for restoration to reduce floods
stories.summary: Authorities in Tennessee, US, have acquired 985 acres along the South Fork of the Forked Deer River to reduce flooding and restore natural habitats. The river was straightened in 1916 to drain surrounding land, but the changes contributed to flash floods and erosion. The restoration project aims to reconnect the river with its floodplain and eventually open the area to the public.

stories.title: A new fossil from China may reveal the first amphibian known to have lived entirely at sea; the armoured, 2.4-foot creature lived about 237 million years ago, challenging what scientists know about amphibian evolution
stories.summary: A recent discovery of the fossil Gerrothorax maritimus reveals that some ancient amphibians lived completely in marine environments. Dated to approximately 237 million years ago, this species had a flattened body covered in bony armour. The fossils were found in deep-sea sediments, indicating they lived far from landmasses. Geochemical tests confirmed the strontium isotopes matched those in seawater during the Late Triassic period.

stories.title: 'PM Modi, Amit Shah suffering loss': Sanjay Raut on business concerns of traders ahead of INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: Sanjay Raut asserted that the rally by the INDIA bloc in Delhi would not disrupt business activities. He emphasized that this event signifies the people's demand for a change in government. Supporters of various political parties began gathering for the rally, which aims to address alleged voter roll tampering. The demonstration is expected to attract significant participation amid security measures by the police.

stories.title: 'India not a banana republic': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: Union minister JP Nadda accused Congress and Rahul Gandhi of attempting to destabilize the government and create unrest. Nadda labeled the opposition's rally at Ramlila Maidan as a calculated conspiracy against democracy and the economy. He outlined a model of politics involving misinformation and provoking protests. The INDIA bloc, however, claims to mobilize for democratic rights concerning alleged electoral roll irregularities.

stories.title: 'No military solutions': EAM Jaishankar reveals PM Modi-Putin talks on Ukraine conflict in Delhi, Bishkek
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar conveyed India's diplomatic commitment regarding the Ukraine conflict during discussions in Atlanta. His talks included priorities such as protecting civilian shipping and restoring crucial grain exports. Jaishankar also emphasized the need for energy security in light of ongoing disruptions. He met with counterparts from Russia, Poland, and South Korea to address bilateral and multilateral issues.

stories.title: Ohio couple splits before marriage, court awards woman $41,466 from house sale
stories.summary: An Ohio man who refused to share money from his house sale with his former partner has lost a court battle. The couple had signed an agreement in 2021 to divide the proceeds if the property was sold. After their breakup, the man argued that the woman had not spent enough on renovations. However, an appeals court upheld the agreement, awarding her $41,466.50.

stories.title: ‘A hurry to finish JD(U)’: RJD's Manoj Jha on MLCs who defeated Nitish's party joining BJP
'Remarkable valour': PM Modi pays tribute to Haryana's heritage on foundation day
stories.summary: Celebrating its 60th Foundation Day on November 1, Haryana showcased its rich heritage and remarkable achievements. Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the state's vital role in agriculture, sports, and defense. Political leaders such as Amit Shah and Rahul Gandhi commended Haryana's vibrant culture. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini spoke about the significant progress over the decades.

stories.title: Fat-dissolving claims land FatX Solution in regulatory trouble; CDSCO cancels registration
North Korea tests new cluster-bomb warhead under Kim Jong-un's military push
Texas Supreme Court Blocks Neighbours’ Broad Demand to Inspect Woman’s 14-Acre Homestead
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, the Texas Supreme Court has sided with Pamela Bosco, affirming her right to keep her 14-acre homestead intact. The court denied neighbors’ requests for property inspections due to insufficient evidence of alleged violations. This ruling underscores the importance of legal processes in property disputes and confirms that establishing wrongdoing necessitates proper evidence gathering.

stories.title: ‘It was Nehru Ji’s chair’: Cong reveals significance of seat used by Meira Kumar during CEC’s public impeachment
1 killed, several injured in shooting at US stadium after Alabama football game
‘Don’t just protest, shop’: Rahul urges INDIA bloc rally to support Delhi traders
'Fair of Thugs': BJP takes swipe at opposition with poster ahead of massive INDIA bloc rally
stories.summary: As the INDIA bloc prepares for its rally, the Delhi unit of BJP has launched a poster campaign aimed at opposition leaders. This rally is centered on demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over perceived electoral discrepancies. Many protesters from different states have arrived to raise concerns about the electoral process, particularly regarding Electronic Voting Machines.

stories.title: Atlanta Quad Meeting: Jaishankar seeks action‑oriented agenda; bloc unveils AI, minerals push
stories.summary: During the Quad meeting, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar highlighted the significance of preserving freedom of choice and ensuring secure supply chains. The dialogue centered around addressing non-market practices impacting the Indo-Pacific, without naming specific nations. The ministers unveiled plans to enhance access to artificial intelligence and aid critical minerals recovery while condemning issues like human trafficking and online fraud, pledging to collaboratively combat transnational crimes.

stories.title: 'GenZ regelt!' Thousands protest across Germany in Halloween costumes
Six Indian tourists go missing during trek to Nepal's Shey-Phoksundo Lake
Iran Sees US Letter As Victory: Rezaei hails softer tone as win; Khamenei warns of retaliation
stories.summary: Iran's influential security figure Mohsen Rezaei noted a shift in the US's approach toward Tehran, interpreting this as a triumph for the Iranian populace. In reaction, foreign minister Abbas Araghchi expressed optimism about potential negotiations, agreeing with the analysis of recent communications. Simultaneously, Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei cautioned against threats from the US or Israel, while President Trump maintained that Iran is keen to engage, hinting at an imminent meeting.

stories.title: Trump speaks to Netanyahu as US weighs fresh military strikes on Iran: Report

stories.summary: After an extensive search, the West Valley Muslim Association has successfully acquired a property in Cupertino for $16.5 million. This new facility will serve as a permanent home for the community, offering a venue for daily prayers, educational activities, and community gatherings. Supported by a dedicated fundraising campaign, this purchase reflects the growing needs of the local Muslim population, establishing a vital center for faith and fellowship.

stories.title: Mumbai gets its first nuclear science school at HSNC University
3,700-year-old man buried with stone in his mouth beneath a hearth may have been part of magical ritual
stories.summary: Approximately 3,700 years ago, a man in southeastern Spain underwent a burial unlike any other. Researchers suggest that this ritual may have been intended to symbolically overcome a threat rather than inflict punishment. The discovery of his body underneath a hearth, with a stone in his mouth, implies an effort to silence him.

stories.title: How UKHarvest turned food waste into 10 million meals
stories.summary: In 2017, Yvonne Thomson founded UKHarvest to address food waste and assist individuals facing food insecurity. Initially starting with one van, the charity has impressively salvaged 10 million meals throughout its journey. Its initiatives, including Community Food Hubs and Grub Clubs, offer not only affordable food but also valuable education. Collecting about 10 tonnes of excess food weekly, UKHarvest enjoys the patronage of Queen Camilla, amplifying its community impact.

stories.title: If you hire H-1B, you won't get grants: Texas Agriculture Department's new rule for businesses; 'Taxpayers work hard for their money'
Jammu & Kashmir HC strikes down water tax on hydropower projects
A helicopter with the EU force in Bosnia crashes, reportedly killing 3 and injuring 12
UT students wanted to condemn comments targeting Indian-origin students but university thought it was not just Bo French
Antipodes Island Sees Ground Beetle Numbers Surge 40-Fold After Mice Eradication
stories.summary: The successful removal of invasive house mice from Antipodes Island has spurred a remarkable resurgence in ground beetle populations, which have increased to around 40 times their former numbers. This ecological transformation highlights the beneficial effects of eradicating invasive species, fostering a healthier food web and aiding in the survival of native bird species. Long-term observation is crucial for comprehending the recovery dynamics of island ecosystems.

stories.title: Texas’s Historic Imperial Sugar Char House Gets $15M Rescue After 20 Years Vacant
stories.summary: Sugar Land City Council has given a green light for a $15 million initiative to safeguard the iconic Imperial Sugar Char House. This undertaking aims to stabilize the structure and prevent further deterioration over the years ahead. Work is set to commence shortly, with an anticipated completion by 2028. Officials are still finalizing plans for potential future utilizations, leaving residents eager for tangible development on this cherished landmark.

stories.title: SIR deadlines extended in 5 states, Delhi; EC sets new dates for final rolls
$410M plan to transform Connecticut power plant into waterfront park
Jamia sets date for student union poll, revokes disciplinary action against protesters
'Transgressions by China happen, it's not new': Arunachal CM says no intrusion along LAC
stories.summary: Pema Khandu asserted that border transgressions along the India-China frontier have been a longstanding issue, highlighting China's non-recognition of the McMahon Line. He described the recent confrontations as transgressions instead of intrusions and reassured citizens of the state's stability. Likewise, Union tourism minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat reaffirmed the safety of India's borders while working to alleviate media-induced tensions regarding the situation.

stories.title: Taking antibiotics? Eating a lot of sugar at the same time may make the damage to your gut worse, scientists have found, suggesting that what you eat during a course of antibiotics could affect how well your body recovers
stories.summary: Research findings indicate that a diet high in sugar can significantly affect the diversity of gut bacteria in patients undergoing antibiotic therapy. The study monitored the food intake and gut microbiome of hospitalized cancer patients treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, revealing a strong connection between elevated sugar levels and shifts in gut bacteria.

stories.title: In 1987, an amateur fossil hunter found a T. rex in South Dakota; the $31.8 million skeleton now stands in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: In 1987, Stan Sacrison found a T. rex skeleton in South Dakota, which was later sold for $31.8 million. Initially misidentified, the bones were correctly recognized as belonging to a T. rex in 1992. After years at the Black Hills Institute, the skeleton was auctioned and purchased for a museum in Abu Dhabi. Stan is now displayed in a dramatic scene depicting conflicts with another T. rex.

stories.title: 'Keeping a list of names': Abhishek Banerjee warns cops trying to 'please' Suvendu
Texas Jury Finds No Legal or Informal Adoption in $1 Million Inheritance Dispute
stories.summary: In a complex Texas inheritance case, a stepson referred to as 'my child' in a will navigated a treacherous dispute following his father's passing. Despite his claims of informal adoption, the family remained unconvinced. Ultimately, the jury affirmed that no formal or informal adoption occurred. This outcome highlights the necessity of clear legal documentation in estate planning to avoid misunderstandings, particularly within blended families concerning rights to inheritance.

stories.title: Steven Spielberg pulls $29.9 M LA ranch off the market
stories.summary: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg listed his Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million but has now taken it off the market. He and his wife purchased the property in 1999 for $5.75 million, intending to create equestrian facilities. After facing opposition from local residents, their renovation plans were significantly reduced over the years. The ranch, known as Dogwood, features a main house with numerous upscale amenities and a 20,000-square-foot riding arena.

stories.title: In 1600, William Gilbert called Earth a giant magnet; his book sold for Rs 58.5 lakh in 2026
stories.summary: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.

stories.title: In 2022, conservators X-raying a Van Gogh painting in Edinburgh found a hidden self-portrait of the artist on the back of the canvas, concealed for more than a century under layers of glue and cardboard
stories.summary: A self-portrait of Vincent van Gogh was discovered concealed behind another painting after many years. The hidden portrait was found during routine examinations ahead of an exhibition. This discovery highlights Van Gogh's habit of reusing canvases due to financial difficulties throughout his life. Conservators are now working to reveal the portrait without damaging the original painting. Visitors to the exhibition were able to view the hidden portrait's X-ray image.

stories.title: Netanyahu's unity government gambit: Can he lure Eisenkot from opposition?
Trump official reacts to leaked video of Microsoft's AI chief telling staff company wants to bring foreign talents: 'You were hoping we were kidding'
Texas homeowners win control of their park, roads and ponds after a decade-long legal battle
stories.summary: In a significant turn of events, residents of La Bota Ranch in Laredo officially gained control over common property areas after a protracted legal battle. This shift follows a jury's March 2022 decision that found developers had breached fiduciary duties, prompting residents to reevaluate governance due to rising association fees. The final handover on August 20, 2026, empowers homeowners over shared facilities, symbolizing a hard-won victory for community representation.

stories.title: 'Don't push us': SC warns of harsh stand on firecrackers if orders go unenforced
stories.summary: The Supreme Court tackled the persistent air pollution crisis in Delhi-NCR, stressing the importance of adhering to current firecracker laws. Authorities were cautioned against inaction, as deteriorating air quality poses a threat to public health. The bench underlined the necessity for collaboration among all parties to effectively manage firecracker usage. Measures taken by the Delhi government include restrictions on older vehicles and staggered work hours.

stories.title: A 3,106-carat diamond pulled from a South African mine became the 530-carat gem in Britain's royal sceptre
stories.summary: Frederick Wells discovered the enormous Cullinan diamond in South Africa in 1905 while working at the Premier Mine. Its exceptional size caught public attention, leading to its purchase by the Transvaal government for King Edward VII. The diamond was carefully cut into several gemstones over eight months, resulting in noteworthy pieces for the British royal collection. Following Edward VII's death, the largest stone was incorporated into the Sovereign's Sceptre.

stories.title: An Indy charity started in 2016 with $9k raised in 45 mins; 10 yrs on, it reached 175k bouquets
stories.summary: Random Acts of Flowers Indianapolis marked ten years of service, delivering its 175,000th flower arrangement to Eskenazi Health. This charity reuses donated flowers to create arrangements for hospital patients in need. Volunteers collect flowers from various local sources to prevent waste and support emotional well-being. The organization was founded after a successful fundraising effort in 2016. It aims to continue its work through community partnerships and ongoing donations.

stories.title: Newly identified bird like dinosaur from Cretaceous period may be first dinosaur eating fruit
stories.summary: Scientists have recently uncovered a small dinosaur named Infernogallus jamesi, believed to have predominantly dined on fruit. By examining its skull and jaw muscles, researchers gained insights into its dietary habits. Existing during the Cretaceous period, as flowering plants flourished, this dinosaur displays anatomical traits akin to modern fruit-feeding parrots, deepening our comprehension of the varied lifestyles in the era of dinosaurs.

stories.title: 'Educated voters don't turn up in assembly polls': UP minister OP Rajbhar plays down MLC results
Royal regret! British king 'recognises' slavery horrors amid his Caribbean tour
stories.summary: Despite the pressure, Buckingham Palace has said Charles will not issue an apology during the tour, arguing that such matters are “matters for governments to address”. The palace added that he would “not shy away from the darkest days of our past.” As monarch, Charles represents Britain abroad on the advice of the government.

stories.title: The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago may have also set the stage for ants to conquer the planet, with scientists finding a surprising boost from so-called jumping genes hidden in ant DNA
stories.summary: Since the dinosaurs vanished, ants have flourished, with more than 15,000 species recognized globally. New research, spearheaded by Dr. Lukas Schrader, highlights the role of jumping genes in their evolution and resilience. Significant surges of these genes occurred during the early Paleogene period, enhancing ants' olfactory receptors and social communication skills, thus providing a genetic edge for survival in diverse environments.

stories.title: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show clear signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists have found an important clue hidden in a rare group of resilient brains
stories.summary: Recent research from the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience has revealed intriguing findings about Alzheimer's disease. Scientists examined brain tissues from different groups, including those with and without dementia symptoms. They discovered that immature neurons acted differently in cognitively healthy individuals despite Alzheimer's brain changes. This suggests that these neurons may play a role in supporting brain function rather than simply replacing damaged cells.

stories.title: He wrote a book on 'Black Money', Feds tracked his $900K loan fraud: Indian-origin accountant jailed in Texas, investigator says 'I can only imagine his shock...'
University of Florida seeks an H-1B for a financial analyst, president Bell says it was made without his approval
MLC poll setback opens new front within Mahayuti; Shinde-for-CM pitch, 'Shakuni mama' jibe fly
'Double loss of double engine': Akhilesh mocks BJP over UP MLC poll results
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav criticized the BJP following their loss in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections held recently. He attributed the victory to teachers and young voters while alleging electoral manipulation by the BJP. The Samajwadi Party leader believes this defeat sets the foundation for the upcoming 2027 assembly elections. Yadav emphasized unity among marginalized communities and expressed gratitude towards supporters for their vigilance during the counting process.

stories.title: Mississippi father gives wife home promised to three children; daughter loses court battle
stories.summary: A Mississippi father left his family home and 0.86 acres of land equally to his three children in a 2008 will but transferred the property to his wife in 2021. After his death, his daughter challenged the transfer, claiming he had been improperly influenced due to his declining health. On Tuesday, an appeals court rejected her challenge, finding insufficient evidence of undue influence.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Pakistani lawmaker mocks Khawaja Asif after Munir’s Iran visit; SC wonders what's 'wrong' with victims of digital arrest & more
Wildlife traffickers may have killed her family to capture her; rescued baby gorilla Bili begins a second life in Congo
stories.summary: Bili, the young gorilla saved from wildlife trafficking in Nigeria, has embarked on a fresh journey in the Republic of the Congo. After three years of dedicated care and rehabilitation, she is now set for a quarantine period at the Tchimpounga Nature Reserve. Here, Bili will undergo health assessments and prepare for her introduction to fellow gorillas, with hopes of eventually reintegrating her into the wild.

stories.title: Minecraft creator lists Beverly Hills estate for $70M
stories.summary: Markus 'Notch' Persson has placed his Beverly Hills mansion on the market for $70 million. He purchased the estate in 2014 after outbidding Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who also showed interest. The mansion features eight bedrooms, a nightclub, and a professional recording studio for entertainment. The billionaire decided to sell as he spends less time in Los Angeles these days.

stories.title: India-EU landmark FTA likely rollout in mid-2027, says top EU lawmaker
British woman collects 4,550 My Little Pony items after being denied a horse
It only takes one rumour: How a small trigger can lead to a deadly stampede
stories.summary: On October 17, a tragic stampede in Kolkata claimed 19 lives during the Durga Puja celebrations. The incident was caused by overcrowding, panic, and a misleading announcement about structural failure. Experts emphasize the importance of effective crowd management to prevent similar tragedies in the future. Investigators are examining various factors contributing to the disaster, including narrow exits and inadequate safety measures.

stories.title: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum's $36 million donation helps expand Los Angeles Jewish school
stories.summary: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum's $36 million donation has helped Milken Community School open a new campus in Bel Air, Los Angeles, for students in grades 9 to 12. Inaugurated on Sunday, the campus has expanded the school's total footprint to 28 acres across three locations. The opening comes as the school reports a 40% rise in applications.

stories.title: 'What is wrong with victims': CJI on digital arrest cases; calls for compensation from banks
SC disposes of Mahua Moitra's plea seeking public disclosure of AIF, FPI beneficiaries
4-year-old Tennessee boy donates $150 from lemonade stand to soup kitchen
From Hitler’s rise to farmers’ misery in India: How the Great Depression changed lives far beyond America
stories.summary: The October 1929 stock market crash in the United States ignited a global economic disaster that resulted in widespread unemployment and business closures. In Germany and India, the crisis led to heightened political unrest and movements for independence. Falling agricultural prices devastated Indian farmers, pushing them closer to revolution against British oppression. Meanwhile, Britain faced significant industrial downturns and job losses, highlighting the urgent need for international economic collaboration.

stories.title: Sneako reportedly sends legal demand to Akademiks over post about alleged intimate video threat
stories.summary: DJ Akademiks’ platform recently revealed threatening claims involving potential release of intimate videos related to Sneako, which arose from a group call conflict. The legal notification regarding these video allegations lacks independent verification, casting doubt on its legitimacy. Despite a request to eliminate the post, Akademiks TV stood firm on their reporting rights.

stories.title: MLC election results: BJP wins big, but Congress and Samajwadi Party send a message from Nagpur, Varanasi
stories.summary: While the BJP-led NDA won big in the MLC elections across four states, it suffered setbacks in two politically significant constituencies: Nagpur and Varanasi where the Congress and SP held their ground.

stories.title: NJ homeowner challenged neighbour's plunge pool over flooding; appeals court upheld case dismissal
stories.summary: In Toms River, New Jersey, a family contested a neighbour's pool due to flooding fears. David Faloba represented his parents in challenging the project, citing environmental concerns. The court found the DEP had approved the pool based on compliance with relevant regulations. The appellate court upheld the dismissal of Faloba's lawsuit, emphasizing correct legal processes were not followed.

stories.title: Gavin Newsom-linked San Francisco cottage sells for $5.85 million, up from $2.8 million in 2019
stories.summary: A beautifully preserved redwood cottage in San Francisco, formerly owned by the family of Gavin Newsom, has recently fetched $5.85 million at sale. Initially on the market for $4.5 million, the residence located in Cole Valley drew numerous cash offers, driven largely by its spacious potential and the allure tied to its former ownership.

stories.title: ‘This is the future you want?’ White House cites France riots to slam Democrats ahead of midterms
stories.summary: In France, recent demonstrations regarding education and living costs have spiraled into significant unrest and violence. Initially sparked by issues in educational facilities, the protests quickly broadened to encompass widespread frustration with public services. The Trump administration seizes upon these events to castigate Democrats, linking them to growing disorder in America.

stories.title: US releases rare image of China's secretive space plane docked to another spacecraft
stories.summary: A US military intelligence agency has released a rare photograph of China's secretive Shenlong space plane, showing it attached to another spacecraft in orbit. Taken in May 2024 and made public in October 2026, the image reveals its open payload bay and another satellite with extended solar panels. However, the purpose of the connection remains unknown.

stories.title: Why did Kick suspend Vitaly after his latest livestream? Here’s what we know
stories.summary: Recently, streamer Vitaly faced suspension from Kick due to breaches of the platform's endangerment policies during his 'Catching Predators IRL' livestream featuring Lil Pump. While the suspension email referenced specific evidence, it failed to clarify the exact reasons behind the decision. Past incidents related to his controversial predator-catching streams have sparked debate about his approach, and there is still uncertainty regarding the length of the suspension and possible reinstatement.

stories.title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback
'Vote chori' row: INDIA bloc to hold 'mock Parliament' to 'impeach' CEC Gyanesh Kumar; mega rally on Nov 1
Wendy Schmidt's $1.4 million oil-cleanup challenge after Deepwater Horizon
Minnesota neighbours lose $148,500 award as court settles nine-year lake access dispute
stories.summary: A nine-year property dispute over access to Minnesota's Prairie Lake has taken another turn after an appeals court upheld a ruling in favour of the Blackwood Trust. The Monday decision confirms the trust's direct access to the lake and leaves an earlier $148,500 trespass award to neighbouring property owners cancelled. The dispute centred on conflicting land surveys dating back to 1997.

stories.title: 10-year-old Georgia boy raises $400 selling bracelets to help homeless people
A vitamin clue to stroke in the young? Bengaluru study finds low B6 levels
stories.summary: A recent study from Bengaluru finds lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults with ischaemic strokes compared to healthy individuals. This study involved comparing vitamin B6 levels in 171 stroke patients and 249 healthy controls. Researchers found that vitamin B6 insufficiency was more prevalent among stroke patients than in the control group. Although vitamin B6 is linked to stroke risk, further research is essential to understand the implications.

stories.title: Congress calls Rahul Gandhi's 'Sitarama' misspelling in Tata post 'typo marketing', mocks BJP
Thousands of years of knowledge, struggle shaped India as cultural nation: Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
stories.summary: At the launch of 'Timeless India' held at Dharohar Bhawan, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat passionately articulated the essence of India's cultural heritage, which has been shaped through centuries of learning and trials. This book is a clarion call for the preservation of our historical sites and a deeper understanding of our cultural narrative.

stories.title: Demolition damaged Miami home in 2014; Florida court upholds woman's $240,000 insurance victory after 12 years
stories.summary: In Florida, Sandra Moise faced significant challenges when her home was damaged due to vibrations from nearby demolition activities. Initially, her insurance provider, Homeowners Choice, denied her claim citing policy exclusions against earth movement. After enduring a prolonged legal battle, a jury ultimately sided with her, confirming the damage's cause.

stories.title: At 62, Marcelle Flowers feared AI until two young founders changed her career
California couple's garden dispute ends in court after 1955 deal involving $250 and babysitting
stories.summary: A California couple who bought a home in 2019 found themselves in a legal battle after their neighbour claimed ownership of a 20-by-20-foot garden they believed was theirs. The dispute centred on a 1955 agreement involving $250, babysitting services and land access rights. On Monday, a California appeals court upheld the couple's exclusive right to use the garden.

stories.title: US midterms: FBI, ICE agents will not serve as election monitors, DOJ says
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice has decided that FBI personnel will not oversee polling sites during upcoming elections. Concerns were raised regarding potential intimidation of voters, especially from minority communities. Civil rights groups, led by the NAACP, filed a lawsuit to prevent federal law enforcement at polling places. Federal election monitors will be present but will not have law enforcement powers.

stories.title: Forces fortify key Arunachal bridge to fight dam objectors
stories.summary: Protests against the dam at the Dite-Dime bridge have prompted a strong response from law enforcement. The Central Armed Police Forces have been deployed to ensure order in the affected districts. Recent confrontations during a bandh left several people injured, including four women, escalating tensions. As supporters clashed with security, the Dite-Dime bridge emerges as a focal point of strife near the India-China border.

stories.title: Washington appeals court upholds anti-harassment order after neighbour allegedly disrupts utilities
stories.summary: A dispute between a couple and their neighbour escalated into serious harassment concerning driveway access and utilities. The couple claimed that their neighbour blocked the shared driveway and cut off their water supply. This pattern of interference led them to seek legal protection from the court. The Washington Court of Appeals confirmed that their claims warranted an anti-harassment order.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Amit Shah speaks to four CMs, says relief operations on 'war footing'
stories.summary: Amidst the aftermath of Cyclone Arnab, Union home minister Amit Shah coordinated efforts with chief ministers of the impacted states, pledging essential assistance to alleviate the disaster's effects. With nine fatalities reported in Andhra Pradesh, evacuations were necessary, and significant crop damage affected about 2 lakh hectares. Restoration work is underway, with unwavering support from the central government for the affected regions.

stories.title: An animal-borne virus called Shamonda, which normally circulates in livestock, has infected and killed a human for the first time
stories.summary: A 61-year-old man in France has tragically lost his life to the Shamonda virus, a disease previously only observed in animals. The man, who was battling leukaemia, contracted the virus likely through a midge bite. With documented cases of infected animals in Europe and previous outbreaks in Africa and Asia, health officials are investigating how the virus spreads and its possible risks to humans.

stories.title: North Carolina city restores 27 acres of wetlands to reduce flood risks for 93 properties
stories.summary: Hendersonville celebrates the successful completion of the first phase of its Lower Mud Creek Floodplain Restoration Project. This significant endeavor aims to mitigate flood risks for surrounding properties, boosting community safety. Key efforts include reconnecting Mud Creek with its floodplain to enhance water quality and flood management. Financial support from various organizations has been crucial in the project's design and construction.

stories.title: Henry F. Porter Preserve Deal: 181 acres permanently protected; cross-border pact links key habitats
stories.summary: A groundbreaking conservation project has successfully preserved 181 acres of forests and wetlands straddling Maryland and Delaware. Championed by the Porter family alongside multiple conservation entities, the Henry F. Porter Preserve focuses on safeguarding vital ecosystems. This initiative not only emphasizes sustainable practices but also plays a pivotal role in the overall protection of the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

stories.title: 'Don't worry about lathis': Rahul calls on people to join INDIA bloc's 'Delhi chalo' march
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi invited everyone to partake in the upcoming Chalo Delhi march at Ramlila Maidan. This initiative seeks to challenge purported electoral malfeasance and uphold democratic integrity. He stated the march embodies the nation’s collective desire and is open to all political groups. Student bodies from throughout the political spectrum are encouraged to join. The Congress party plans a significant opposition rally on November 1.

stories.title: Michigan appeals court upholds $9.7 million verdict after mother dies following tummy tuck surgery
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, a Michigan court has affirmed a nearly $9.7 million ruling against Henry Ford Macomb Hospital for negligence that led to Cathleen Allen's tragic death after cosmetic surgery complications. Medical testimony highlighted that prompt action could have preserved her life. The jury attributed liability to both the surgeon and hospital, underscoring the urgent need for stringent patient safety measures.

stories.title: ‘From Varanasi to Nagpur’: Congress' Jairam Ramesh says voters reject PM Modi govt’s policies
US company’s patent bid for life-saving TB therapy nixed
Junk food’s impact may go beyond the weighing scale
'Fadnavis forced to delete tweet': Congress takes swipe at Maharashtra CM after win in Nagpur MLC polls
'Never knew he was dangerous’: Kiren Rijiju reacts to Naseeruddin Shah's 'dimagi naxal' post
‘Unwavering commitment’: Rajnath Singh backs ASEAN centrality, calls for stronger defence ties
JeI functionary met Indian intel official in secret: Bangladesh PM aide
MEA says 22 Indians killed during West Asia conflict
'From the river to the sea': Hundreds rally across Israel advocating Jewish-Arab gov
stories.summary: Around 300 demonstrators gathered in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, and Haifa to demand a Jewish-Arab government. Protesters held signs advocating for freedom and inclusive governance, reflecting their unified call. The demonstrations coincided with ongoing vote counting following Israel's closely contested election. Pro-Netanyahu parties secured 53 seats, while the opposing bloc held 48, leaving no clear majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot emphasized a need for change, criticizing Netanyahu's government.

stories.title: Supreme Court removes October 30 deadline for additions to Delhi electoral roll
Isro to launch NVS-03 on Oct 30, but NavIC has a long way to go
IN-SPACe picks 6 AI space projects for grants of up to Rs 1-cr each
Sunshine Buns, started in 2022 by four Utah friends, raised $7 million
stories.summary: Sunshine Buns has successfully secured $7 million in Series A funding, allowing them to broaden their store presence. Founded by four friends using a family cinnamon roll recipe, their frozen delights are now featured in major retailers like Target and Costco. This new funding will support production and marketing efforts, and the founders attribute their success to local mentors and the nurturing startup community in Utah.

stories.title: Guess how many Congress won: PM Modi
Healthy citizens essential to achieve goal of developed India: Anupriya Patel
Arab parties claim kingmaker status in Israel elections
stories.summary: Joint list open to Eisenkot minority government; Ra'am's Abbas says 'everyone talking to us'

stories.title: Diver searching the bottom of England’s River Wear has pulled a huge three legged iron cauldron
stories.summary: An ancient iron cauldron, potentially from the medieval or Iron Age, was found submerged under water. Underwater archaeologist Gary Bankhead led a team of divers in this ambitious recovery mission. Experts are currently investigating the cauldron's design and historical relevance. This intriguing find prompts speculation about its origin and journey into the river, with plans underway for a public exhibition at a nearby museum.

stories.title: Megan Fox settled $5M Malibu home lawsuit for $100K after three-year fight
Florida man pays HOA debt five days after home auction; court overturns sale cancellation
stories.summary: A Florida homeowner paid his outstanding homeowners' association fees five days after his property was sold at a foreclosure auction in October 2024. The sale was subsequently cancelled, but the winning bidder challenged the decision, saying it had not been heard. Nearly two years later, a Florida appeals court overturned the cancellation and ordered a fresh hearing.

stories.title: Israel poll results deadlocked amid historic showing by Arab parties
Monitor welfare schemes closely: PM Modi to chief secretaries
SC summons Sanjay Raut in contempt case
Yet to test legality of logical discrepancy in SIR: Supreme Court
Historian Charles Greig donated 50 paintings and watercolours to Tate; from colonial India
stories.summary: In a remarkable gesture, Tate London has received a donation of 50 artworks from the British colonial era in India, showcasing the talents of both Indian and European artists. This diverse collection, meticulously curated by British art historian Charles Greig over 40 years, will be publicly exhibited at Tate Britain in 2028, enhancing public access to these invaluable historical pieces and underscoring the importance of art preservation.

stories.title: Texas barber returns $128,514 found at ATM despite rent struggles
stories.summary: In Lewisville, Texas, a barber stumbled upon two bags at an ATM, one filled with an astonishing $128,514 in cash. Struggling with rent and financial issues, he made the commendable choice to report this to the authorities. The bags belonged to a Brink’s team who had accidentally left them behind. Though no financial reward was given, the barber's honesty was recognized and celebrated by the police.

stories.title: Georgia siblings fight over 95-year-old mother's care and assets; court backs daughter
stories.summary: A dispute between three siblings over their 95-year-old mother's care reached the Georgia Court of Appeals after one son restricted his sister's visits and questions emerged over the handling of their mother's money. The woman, who has advanced dementia, had previously authorised her son to manage her affairs. However, the court upheld her daughter's appointment as guardian.

stories.title: NDA wins 1 6 of 28 seats, Congress falters in MLC polls
Rahul lashes out at government over Tatas, FM Nirmala Sitharaman hits back
In SC, biological women oppose equal rights for transgender women
Vance tests diplomatic route to Iran as Trump weighs escalation
The UK plans to send giant robotic claws into orbit to grab two dead satellites; 2029 mission
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking initiative, the UK plans to unveil a pioneering spacecraft in 2029, designed specifically for the cleanup of space debris. Utilizing advanced robotic arms, the mission aims to snatch up and incinerate inactive satellites, tackling the escalating issue of orbital pollution that threatens current satellite operations. A nationwide competition to name the spacecraft is in progress, underscoring the project's significance in fostering sustainable space practices.

stories.title: Delhi HC rejects PIL against passport fee hike for NRIs
Maui Estate Fetches $18.5 Million: Renovated Makena home tops 2026 sale; big price cut reflects cooling market
stories.summary: Recently, a stunning oceanfront estate in Makena, Maui, fetched a remarkable $18.5 million. After undergoing extensive renovations to boost its allure, this property saw an adjustment in its listing price from an initially higher value. While Hawaii's ultra-luxury housing market, especially for homes over $10 million, has been experiencing a downturn, this sale highlights ongoing interest in distinctive coastal properties.

stories.title: To empower panchayats, gram yojana gets nod
Two California brothers face 35 felony charges each after hundreds complain of unfinished homes
stories.summary: A retired nurse in California paid more than $40,000 in 2023 for a backyard home that was never built. The company, Anchored Tiny Homes, later faced more than 200 complaints across 18 counties over unfinished projects and missing payments. Its founders, brothers Austin and Colton Paulhus, now face 35 felony charges each, while affected homeowners remain uncertain about recovering their money.

stories.title: Centre’s Diwali gift to pensioners, staff: 3% DA hike
Flávio Bolsonaro claims Brazil election fraud, declares himself ‘true president-elect’
Privacy law doesn’t infringe upon press freedom: IT & I&B minister

In 2012 and 2013, Maine removed two old Penobscot River dams to restore migratory routes; by September 2026, the Milford fish lift had counted a preliminary 5.85 million river herring returning upstream
stories.summary: In a significant ecological feat, the Penobscot River restoration in Maine has revitalized migratory fish numbers dramatically. As a result, the population of river herring has surged from just 556 to over 5 million.

stories.summary: A long-hidden jewellery collection from Worcestershire unexpectedly fetched £506,750 at auction, surpassing the initial estimate of £150,000. This remarkable sale featured over 200 items, captivating global bidders. Among them, a rare brooch and necklace attracted particularly fierce competition, reflecting their exceptional quality. Profits from this auction will be distributed among the heirs of the deceased owner, marking a remarkable conclusion to a decades-long enigma.

Rare Edvard Munch print bought in 1969 resurfaces in England, valued at up to £80,000
stories.summary: On 28 October 2026, Catherine Southon Auctioneers will present an extraordinary woodcut print by Edvard Munch, previously in the possession of a prominent Norwegian family. Titled Melancholy III, this artwork carries an estimated auction price of £50,000 to £80,000, spotlighting its cultural significance. The included sales receipt from Norway, dated back to 1969, provides a rich context, showcasing Munch's unique printmaking methods that enhance its artistic relevance.

stories.title: Indiana mother wins appeal, avoids college costs after son ignored 25 texts over four years
stories.summary: An Indiana appeals court has determined that a mother is not obliged to finance her son's tertiary education, citing four years of estrangement post-family split as decisive. The ruling highlighted that the son's voluntary disengagement from their relationship granted the mother a valid legal defense. Furthermore, the court dismissed the father's appeal as insufficient to impact the prior court's conclusions, reaffirming existing Indiana law on parental responsibilities regarding education.

US charges 48 non-citizens in election-related cases across five states; two Indians named
stories.summary: The US Justice Department has announced charges against 48 non-citizens in election-related cases across Pennsylvania, California, Florida, New York and Nevada. Two Indian nationals are among those accused. The cases involve allegations of illegal voting in federal elections, fraudulent voter registration and false claims of US citizenship, including alleged misrepresentations in naturalisation proceedings. All defendants are presumed innocent.

stories.title: Maine woman wins federal court battle over faulty $189,471 foreclosure notice
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, a federal court upheld that Maine's foreclosure notification regulations extend protections to non-borrowing spouses. This case highlighted a scenario where a woman faced foreclosure due to her husband's refinancing actions, taken without her consent. The lender's notice was found lacking in clarity regarding amounts owed, underscoring the critical need for adherence to state laws which safeguard homeowners from improper foreclosure practices.

stories.title: California river restoration project attracts salmon within days of completion
stories.summary: A remarkable effort in California involved restoration crews who revitalized a section of the Lower Tuolumne River, focusing on creating vital salmon habitats and enriching local biodiversity. The project saw the introduction of over 24,000 cubic yards of gravel and 80 boulders, which collectively improved spawning conditions. Almost immediately after the work was completed, salmon flocked to the newly established habitats, showcasing the project's success.

MIT students tackle lunar waste with recycling system
stories.summary: MIT students have pioneered a revolutionary recycling solution aimed at mitigating waste buildup on the Moon. As new supplies begin to arrive, it is vital to have efficient methods for dealing with packaging waste. This ambitious project, which has garnered accolades from NASA, seeks to transform waste into useful materials for lunar bases, setting a precedent for potential sustainability improvements both on the Moon and Earth.

Georgia businessman jailed for 15 years for $76m Ponzi scheme targeting 300+ investors
stories.summary: Edwin Brant Frost IV, a businessman from Georgia, has received a 15-year prison sentence following his involvement in a Ponzi scheme that deceived more than 300 investors. This fraudulent operation caused a staggering loss of $76 million. Presenting himself as a reliable lender, Frost was actually battling significant financial turmoil. He misappropriated investors' money for his lavish lifestyle and political donations while neglecting loan repayments.

Matthew Brennen, the patient, experienced severe complications that resulted in the removal of his testicle. The jury awarded $9.5 million in damages, recognizing the pain and loss suffered by both Matthew and his wife, Lisa. The defense's arguments regarding testicular torsion were refuted by expert testimony during the trial.
