California court orders removal of 19 ficus trees after roots invade neighbour's property again
stories.summary: In a protracted legal battle between neighboring homeowners in California, the Fourth District Court has decided that the invasive roots of 19 ficus trees must be completely removed. Although a prior financial settlement provided some relief, the roots continued to cause damage, prompting the affected homeowner to seek a more lasting remedy. The court ruled that total removal of the trees was essential to eliminate the persistent nuisance.

Beyoncé’s foundation gives $50,000 to youth charity
stories.summary: In a generous move, Beyoncé’s foundation, BeyGood, has granted $50,000 to In a Perfect World, which concentrates on youth empowerment. This financial support will help expand their educational and leadership initiatives, aiming to reach more young people in need. With its past achievements touching over 50,000 lives worldwide, the organization is crucial in filling the gaps left by funding shortages in schools, striving to uplift disadvantaged communities.

Nina Dobrev and Shaun White’s $4.3 Million Hollywood Hills Home Reportedly Hits Rental Market at $35,000 a Month
stories.summary: In July 2023, Nina Dobrev and Shaun White bought a stunning Hollywood Hills home for $4.3 million. However, after their engagement ended in September 2025, the couple decided to rent out the property for nearly $35,000 per month. This home symbolized their dreams together, but renovations continued even as they faced their separation, leading to complex decisions about their future ownership of the residence.

stories.title: The AI social paradox: Better at communicating, worse at connecting?
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence increasingly influences our daily conversations, providing quick responses and clarifications. While many appreciate its role in easing social interactions, a growing dependency raises concerns about the erosion of personal communication skills and genuine connections. Moreover, the subtleties and emotions that characterize human interaction could potentially be diminished, raising important debates regarding the implications of AI on our relationships.

Cornwall’s Holywell Cave collapses after an overnight cliff fall
stories.summary: Holywell cave, a significant landmark in Cornwall, collapsed after a cliff fall, rendering it inaccessible. This incident occurred overnight and resulted in the area being cordoned off by lifeguards for safety. Local residents and visitors expressed shock at the loss of this iconic site, which featured in the drama Poldark. Many tourists had frequented the cave due to its unique geological formations and connections to popular films.

TOI Youth Icons Summit: CM Yogi highlights UP’s push on jobs, startups and MSMEs, says state now has 25,000 startups
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath highlighted the state's employment initiatives and youth empowerment at the TOI Youth Icons Summit. He emphasized the growth of the startup ecosystem and initiatives for sports-based employment. The chief minister noted the significant increase in MSME units and direct employment opportunities. Additionally, he mentioned plans for Agniveers and employment for young engineers in defense manufacturing.

stories.title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
stories.summary: YSRCP leader YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has publicly acknowledged his mistake of backing the BJP-led NDA government's law to appoint the CEC. Jagan, who was decimated in the 2024 assembly elections, is gearing up to navigate the complicated political landscape as the 2029 elections approach. The court has banned further tree removal and ordered advance notice before irreversible changes. Trump, however, plans to close the 106-year-old course on November 15 despite an ongoing legal challenge.

stories.title: Children aged 7-12 helped tackle cigarette waste on an Ecuador beach;recorded 6,821 fewer butts
stories.summary: In Ecuador's coastal community, children spearheaded a two-year initiative to combat cigarette butt pollution. They collected thousands of butts, leading to a notable reduction along the beach. The project not only educated the youth but also empowered them to engage their families in clean-up campaigns. Local authorities actively supported these efforts, demonstrating the critical role of young voices in tackling environmental issues.

stories.title: Built as a love nest, later linked to a brothel and wartime officers’ club, San Francisco mansion lists for $25 million
stories.summary: Verdier Mansion, nestled in the heart of San Francisco's Russian Hill, is currently listed for $25 million. Built in 1906, this storied property boasts a legacy of scandal, creativity, and mystery. Having changed hands multiple times, it saw significant renovations in 1992, restoring its classic charm. Offering six levels and panoramic city views, the mansion is a unique testament to the neighborhood's vibrant social evolution throughout the years.

Admiral Nelson's archive worth up to £6m goes under the hammer
stories.summary: A collection of 415 historical documents belonging to Vice-Admiral Lord Horatio Nelson is available for auction. Sotheby’s opened bidding on the anniversary of the Battle of Trafalgar and will run until November 18. This collection includes letters to his lover, Emma Hamilton, and significant documents from his military career. The auction is expected to generate between £4 million and £6 million for the Clive Richards Foundation.

He warns that the lawsuit may pry into Kai's personal and professional matters, following allegations from Reggie regarding inappropriate conduct with a young streamer. Kai firmly denies these accusations, and his legal team has responded with a cease-and-desist letter. As the situation escalates, the outcome remains uncertain.

stories.title: Kate Middleton shares new family photo from mountain challenge she took on after cancer treatment
stories.summary: Kate Middleton has shared an unseen photograph featuring Prince William, their three children and mountain rescue volunteers. The picture was taken after she completed Britain's National Three Peaks Challenge in June 2026 to support a cancer charity following her cancer treatment. She posted the photograph on October 25 to mark Mountain Rescue Awareness Day and thank volunteers for their service.

13,800-year-old Alaska campsite reveals tools, a hearth and clues to early life near Beringia
stories.summary: Archaeological research at Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ in Alaska revealed a rich site dating back 13,800 years. The site included stone tools, animal remains, and evidence of a possible shelter. Researchers identified activities such as food processing, toolmaking, and clothing production among early inhabitants. Comparisons with similar tools in Siberia suggest cultural connections across the Bering Land Bridge.

Who named Cyclone Arnab and why? Where it will hit, states on alert and preparedness
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab is intensifying and is forecasted to hit the Andhra Pradesh coastline by Wednesday morning. The India Meteorological Department has issued alerts for severe winds and torrential rainfall affecting multiple states. Emergency shelters and control rooms are set up as beach access is prohibited to ensure public safety. Heavy rains are also impacting Odisha and Jharkhand. Residents are urged to stay updated and minimize travel during the cyclone's effects.

Nearly 30-year-old Magnum Ego ice cream found frozen in 145-year-old Australian store
stories.summary: During a recent freezer renovation in Harrow, Victoria, a shopkeeper stumbled upon a Magnum Ego ice cream believed to be nearly 30 years old. This finding, dating back to the late 1990s, has sparked a wave of nostalgia among Australians reminiscing about their childhood indulgences. Alongside this classic treat, other forgotten snacks like chips and milk containers were also uncovered.

Jon Bon Jovi's Toms River restaurant serves diners facing food insecurity; over 80% of meals went to guests in need in early 2026
stories.summary: In the first half of 2026, JBJ Soul Kitchen in Toms River played a crucial role in combating food insecurity, serving over 15,870 meals at a temporary pop-up. This unique restaurant model fosters a community atmosphere, inviting both paying diners and volunteers to partake in shared meals. Beyond nourishment, it connects individuals with vital resources for housing and mental health support.

stories.title: Texas grandfather wins $93,778 case against grandchildren's mother over unpaid child support
stories.summary: A Texas grandfather who gained custody of his three grandchildren after their father's death in 2017 has won a legal battle against their mother over unpaid child support and medical expenses. On October 23, a Texas appeals court upheld a $93,778 judgment against the mother, including $65,532 in medical costs. The mother had challenged the payments, arguing that the grandfather had not provided sufficient documentation to support his claims.

stories.title: Florida city opens $31 million botanical and wellness park at 209-acre Tucker Ranch preserve
stories.summary: On October 23, 2026, Tucker Ranch Holistic Health and Wellness Park along with its Botanical Garden opened its doors to the public. This remarkable transformation of a former cattle ranch spans 25.6 acres, featuring stunning botanical displays, outdoor fitness spaces, and wellness facilities initiated through a substantial investment. Its mission is to foster health, education, and outdoor engagement for both residents and visitors, with free daily access for all.

Centre to train 10,000 healthcare workers in drug de-addiction by 2029
stories.summary: India's health ministry has initiated a program to train 10,000 healthcare professionals on substance use disorders. The program aims to improve prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of addiction to substances like alcohol and opioids. In the current fiscal year, 2,000 personnel will be trained, with further increments planned over the next two years. Training will be provided through both online and offline methods across various healthcare institutions.

Ed Sheeran performs at New York fundraiser raising $1 million for disadvantaged children in Suffolk
stories.summary: In an inspiring private fundraising gala, Ed Sheeran performed in New York, raising a remarkable $1 million to support disadvantaged children in Suffolk. Local charities will benefit from the funds, which Ipswich Town Football Club chairman Mark Ashton praised. The Lentonbrook Foundation plans to enhance its existing programs for youth in need, ensuring that the community continues to receive vital support.

stories.title: Wyoming landowner’s kitchenless guest house claim rejected by federal appeals court
stories.summary: Gary Binning confronted challenges while trying to build a guest house on his conservation-eased property, as a former Wyoming Supreme Court ruling placed restrictions on residential constructions. Despite his efforts to propose a design without a kitchen in talks with The Nature Conservancy, his idea was rejected due to its multiple residential characteristics. Ultimately, the courts dismissed the case, citing a lack of clarity and reasonable argument in Binning's claims.

stories.title: After 160 years of excavations, archaeologists find a 2,800-year-old bone flute at ancient Troy
stories.summary: For the first time in 160 years, archaeologists unearthed a bone flute at Troy, dating back approximately 2,800 years. In addition, they found a humanoid idol from the Early Bronze Age, offering new insights into the region's cultural traditions. The discoveries were announced by Turkish Minister of Culture and Tourism, Mehmet Nuri Ersoy. This time period correlates with the legendary works of Greek poet Homer.

stories.title: CDC deputy director Jennifer Shuford to exit role after midterms amid vaccine policy changes: Report
stories.summary: Jennifer Shuford, the chief medical officer of the CDC, plans to step down following the midterm elections due to shifts in the Trump administration's vaccine strategy. This new approach introduces a segmented vaccination regimen. Speculations about her exit suggest personal health concerns or differing views on vaccine messaging may have influenced her departure. The CDC and White House have yet to publicly address Shuford's upcoming exit.

Ocean Mixing Barrier Shown: Dye experiment maps slow downward transport; layered structure limits exchange
stories.summary: In a recent experiment near Martha’s Vineyard, scientists introduced rhodamine dye into the Atlantic Ocean to study its behavior. The dye spread quickly in the surface waters but demonstrated a slower descent into deeper layers. Findings showed a marked difference in mixing rates, emphasizing the complexities of ocean stratification on substance movement. This research is vital for the advancement of nutrient and pollutant transport models.

stories.summary: In a legal battle, California resident Wei Shi has taken the City of Palos Verdes Estates to court, claiming excessive delays in the approval of his accessory dwelling unit application. Shi asserts that the city violated state law’s requirements for prompt reviews. Thanks to a favorable ruling from an appeals court, his lawsuit is back on track, seeking over $1 million in damages for these holdups.

New Zealand cat control helps endangered southern dotterels rebound 52% in one year
stories.summary: New Zealand's critically endangered southern dotterel population has risen by 52 percent following focused predator control efforts. Intensive campaigns targeting feral cats on Stewart Island have yielded immediate gains in breeding. The population grew from 105 birds in early 2025 to an estimated 160 in April 2026. Wildlife officials stress that ongoing management of feral cats is crucial for the bird's long-term survival.

California farmer triples walnut revenue by selling directly to 300 customers from a list of 10k
stories.summary: A walnut farmer in California revolutionized his sales with a targeted email marketing campaign. Reaching out to prior cherry customers, he uncovered 300 interested buyers for his walnuts. This approach resulted in his gross revenue tripling against wholesale prices, proving that even a small customer base can boost income stability. Consequently, many farmers are now embracing direct sales strategies to lessen financial uncertainties.

While the 45-room property remains empty, he survives on donated food and clothes, uses power banks to read books on his phone and relies on charity services for essentials. Neighbours have gradually accepted his presence.

stories.title: Man buys box of old medals for £25, discovers rare Captain Cook medal worth £5,000
stories.summary: A man who bought a box of 22 old medals for just £25 at a car-boot sale in West Yorkshire discovered that one was a rare 18th-century medal commemorating Captain James Cook's death in 1779. After selling the other medals for £500, he took the rare piece to an auction house, where it later fetched £5,000. The medal was purchased by the Captain Cook Memorial Museum in Whitby for a special exhibition planned for 2028.

stories.title: Perry Estate Hits Market: Tyler Perry lists $57m Beverly Hills mansion; once home to royal couple
stories.summary: Tyler Perry has listed his Beverly Hills mansion for $57 million amid plans to relocate to Puerto Rico. The estate, known for hosting Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, spans approximately 24,600 square feet. Featuring eight bedrooms and extensive amenities, it offers privacy within the exclusive Beverly Ridge Estates community. She has spent an estimated $194,000 on renovations since June 2024 and hopes to complete most of the work by 2028. As costs could reach $400,000, Anderson describes the project as the biggest gamble of her life.

stories.title: Historic Houston Mansion Listing: 1911 Cleveland home asks $3.995m; price up about 70% from 2015
stories.summary: A remarkable mansion steeped in history, previously tied to the Cleveland family, has hit the market for $3.995 million in Houston. Samoa island sees sea turtles return after invasive animals are removed, restoring wildlife

The eradication of predatory species has also facilitated the revival of native birds, while sea turtles have finally returned to lay their eggs on the island’s shores after years of absence.

The residence boasts a breathtaking 50-meter infinity pool, a fully equipped gym, and expansive outdoor areas for leisure. Recent upgrades include a tennis court and a dirt-bike track, enhancing the estate's allure.

stories.title: Texas man excluded from mother's will loses 70-acre property battle after court ruling
stories.summary: A Texas couple have lost their legal battle to remain on 70 acres of land they say had been in their family for decades. The dispute began after William Dan Moss was excluded from his mother's will. Despite challenging the inheritance decision and subsequent eviction, William and his wife, Brenda, failed to overturn the rulings. On October 22, a Texas appeals court upheld the eviction judgment.

Individuals describe encounters with small figures, a shared vision across multiple cultures. stories.title: Halle Berry helps select filmmakers for Tribeca-Chanel program, awarding $120,000 for a short film

Among the winners were Gem Little and Kseniya Yorsh, awarded for their short film, COWARDS. The program not only offered workshops but also ensured ongoing assistance for project completion. He cited Lal Krishna Advani's collegium system as a potential method for their selection. Oka placed strong emphasis on civil discourse as a pillar of democracy and raised alarms about environmental issues fueling rising temperatures in urban areas like Thane and Mumbai. Additionally, he recommended more efficient uses for public transport funding.

stories.title: Michigan appeals court orders protection order against Arizona father cancelled in custody dispute
stories.summary: A father in Arizona has successfully appealed a protection order placed against him by his child's mother. The Michigan Court of Appeals reversed an earlier court decision and ordered the protection order to be canceled. This dispute arose after the mother moved to Michigan with their child, preventing scheduled parenting time. The appeals court found that the mother did not provide sufficient evidence for the protection order.

stories.title: US court overturns $1.55 million judgment against couple who sought a $150,000 home price cut
stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court has made headlines by overturning a hefty judgment against a couple who backed out of purchasing a luxury residence. Following an inspection that unveiled critical defects, the couple tried to renegotiate the price but ended up facing a breach of contract lawsuit. The trial court had favored the sellers, but the appeals court clarified the buyers' rights regarding inspection clauses, ultimately nullifying the ruling.

This enchanting railroad features tunnels, bridges, and whimsical scale-model towns, captivating visitors of all ages. As a nonprofit organization, it thrives on volunteer support, offering memorable train rides, including a special chair car for those with special needs. Donations and volunteer efforts are vital for its ongoing maintenance and potential expansions.

In 2020, Jeff Robertson’s Halloween display raised $1.1M for St. Jude; 625 homes target $2M in 2026
stories.summary: In 2020, retired Army veteran Jeff Robertson turned his elaborate Halloween skeleton display into a fundraiser for St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital. Skeletons for St. Jude has raised over $1.1 million in six years, with 625 homes expected to participate in 2026. Now in its seventh year, the initiative aims to reach its overall $2 million fundraising goal.

stories.title: A wrong turn in Georgia led an Alabama driver to rescue a sleeping family of 14 from a house fire
stories.summary: A driver named Mr. Casey took a wrong turn in Georgia and discovered a house fire. He alerted the Burke family, which included 14 members, enabling them to escape safely. Despite their escape, the blaze destroyed their home and personal belongings completely. Community support has been overwhelming, with many offering clothing and shelter to the displaced family. The Burkes plan to rebuild and continue fostering children after establishing permanent housing.

Bowl For Ronnie: Ronnie James Dio cancer fund raises over $2m for research
Six Americans sue Trump over WH press restrictions, citing public's right to independent news
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking case, six American citizens have launched a federal lawsuit against President Donald Trump, arguing that his measures restricting journalist access infringe upon the First Amendment. The diverse plaintiffs, comprising journalists, educators, and activists, contend that these selective exclusions compromise the integrity of government reporting. This pivotal case is currently awaiting resolution in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.

stories.title: San Francisco approves auction of $4.4 million vacant home with $340,000 in unpaid taxes and fraud
stories.summary: A luxurious mansion in San Francisco, appraised at $4.4 million, has racked up over $340,000 in unpaid property taxes, prompting the city's Board of Supervisors to initiate a public tax auction. Amidst the backdrop of allegations surrounding forged deeds and ongoing disputes over the vacant residence, local residents have voiced their concerns regarding unauthorized visitors and illicit activities.

stories.title: Vanessa Trump is cancer-free after breast cancer; reveals extreme fatigue was first sign of illness
stories.summary: Vanessa Trump has revealed that extreme fatigue was the first sign of her “very invasive” breast cancer, diagnosed six months ago. Now cancer-free after undergoing a lumpectomy and radiation treatment, she has shared details of her recovery and encouraged people to prioritise their health, schedule regular screenings and understand the importance of early detection.

stories.title: US appeals court rules 10-7 against bond hearings for immigrants detained after illegal entry
stories.summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has made a pivotal ruling concerning immigrant detention, involving three men who unlawfully entered the country. The court decided to overturn earlier decisions that allowed them individualized bond hearings while awaiting removal proceedings. This change stirs substantial dialogue on the potential impacts on the constitutional rights of immigrants facing detention without due process.

stories.title: A 400-year-old Mughal carpet owned by a US financier, novelist and the Thyssen family returns to auction
stories.summary: A remarkable relic from the Mughal era, the 'Yerkes-Remarque' carpet, is set to go under the hammer at Sotheby's. Adorned with intricate hunting scenes and bold motifs from the 17th century, this carpet represents the height of Indian artistry. With previous ownership linked to luminaries like Charles T. Yerkes and Erich Maria Remarque, its historical significance is profound.

stories.summary: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India has issued recommendations for a mandatory authorisation framework for TV distribution services. Stakeholders, including OEMs and broadcasters, will need to comply with new regulations for these applications. A one-time entry fee of Rs 1 lakh and an application processing fee of Rs 10,000 are proposed. These measures aim to protect consumers and ensure accurate TV viewership metrics.

stories.summary: The inauguration of CyRIS by SBI marks a significant step in advancing cybersecurity measures and threat intelligence in finance. Centered around THINK, INNOVATE, and DEFEND, it promotes a cooperative approach among banks, fintechs, and regulators to strengthen resilience. CS Setty, SBI chairman, underscored that bolstering cybersecurity is crucial for maintaining customer trust and proactively addressing threats, alongside regular training for employees and raising customer awareness on digital safety.

stories.title: 25 Arizona voters wrongly flagged by Trump administration regain voting rights days before midterms
stories.summary: Twenty-five US citizens in Arizona have regained their voting access after being wrongly flagged as possible noncitizens. Their registrations were restored following court-ordered mediation between Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap and Attorney General Kris Mayes on October 23. The agreement ended a lawsuit over the restrictions, allowing the affected citizens to vote in the November 3 midterm elections.

Why do people overpay for used cars with mileage just below round numbers?
stories.summary: A recent study showed that used car dealers profit from mileage readings just under round-number thresholds. The researchers analyzed millions of transactions to determine pricing impacts of left-digit bias. Buyers often overlook minor differences in mileage, focusing instead on the first digit. This inattention allows dealers to charge more for cars that appear to be better value.

stories.title: At 17, British student Max Budgen drew 1,300 flipbook pages to set a Guinness World Record
stories.summary: Max Budgen, a 17-year-old student from Petersfield, Hampshire, created a 1,300-page hand-drawn flipbook. He devoted over three weeks to complete this ambitious project while facing challenges. Max experienced boredom and a lack of ideas at times but remained determined to continue. Reaching significant milestones, such as 300 and 1,000 pages, motivated him throughout the process.

stories.title: Irish father loses wedding ring in Italian stream; 3 strangers fly to Ireland to return it
stories.summary: During a delightful family vacation in Italy, an Irish father accidentally lost his wedding ring while enjoying time with his kids. Determined to recover it, his wife enlisted the help of three local good Samaritans who tirelessly searched the river for three days. Miraculously, they located the ring and even journeyed to Ireland to return it personally, forging unexpected bonds between the Irish family and their Italian rescuers.

stories.title: Congress to hold ‘Vote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1; Amit Shah to lead padayatra in T'gana on Nov 2
stories.summary: Congress party president Mallikarjun Kharge announced a rally in New Delhi to protest vote theft allegations. The rally, titled 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao,' aims to challenge the special electoral roll revision process. Meanwhile, BJP leader Amit Shah will participate in a counter-march in Telangana on November 2. The political tension arises from differing accusations regarding electoral irregularities and vote deletions.

stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has denied reports of military tensions concerning potential actions against Iran. Katz stated there are no plans for an attack before the upcoming elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also rejected claims of disagreement with military chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir. In an interview, Netanyahu suggested that he had given instructions regarding the Iranian regime recently.

stories.title: Scarlett Johansson buys $27.5M Manhattan penthouse for $13M
stories.summary: Scarlett Johansson and Colin Jost have purchased a co-op penthouse in Manhattan, which took seven years to sell. The property was initially listed at $27.5 million and underwent several price reductions before the sale. It spans 6,000 square feet and features numerous luxurious amenities, including six bedrooms and seven bathrooms. The previous owners had made extensive renovations before selling, which likely facilitated the eventual sale.

stories.title: BJP protests across states over Kharge's 'baap' remark at PM Modi; demands apology
stories.summary: In response to Mallikarjun Kharge's recent remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi, BJP activists took to the streets in various locations including Bihar, Jammu, and Bengaluru. The protests, spearheaded by local BJP leaders, called for an official apology from Kharge. While Congress rallied behind Kharge, the BJP accused him of demonstrating a lack of respect towards Modi and his family, igniting a national debate on political respect and decorum.

The property, originally listed at $99.5 million, sold for $70.4 million after several price reductions. This 3.18-acre estate features ocean views, a large swimming pool, and a private beach path. Initially acquired by Crawford and her husband in 2015, the home underwent significant renovations before the sale.

stories.title: Sophia Fan, the 17-year-old Maryland student who distributed more than 7,000 books in 4 years

The nonprofit has reached over 7,000 books distributed across multiple states and a chapter in Rwanda. Originally focusing on AP textbooks, it now accepts various types of learning materials. Fan plans to continue this initiative while studying public or global health in college.

stories.title: Alaska Supreme Court blocks gravel mine after years of dispute over noise and bowl-shaped terrain
stories.summary: A gravel mine proposal by Beachcomber LLC in Anchor Point faced strong opposition from local residents. The Kenai Peninsula Borough Planning Commission initially rejected the permit due to significant environmental impact concerns. After several appeals and court rulings, the Alaska Supreme Court upheld the commission's decision in October 2026. The court found substantial evidence showed potential noise and visual disturbances could not be minimized.

stories.title: 'Unforgivable': MP minister Vishvas Sarang slams Kharge over remark on PM Modi

Sarang criticized the need for greater respect towards cultural customs surrounding the deceased, labeling Kharge's comments as wholly unacceptable. He condemned the Congress party's silence on the matter, voicing concern over their current political behavior.

stories.title: 'We hear you': Rahul Gandhi's message to traders in Delhi amid anti-CEC stir
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has publicly backed the traders in Delhi struggling from the ramifications of ongoing protests and governmental restrictions. He pointed fingers at the administration for hampering commerce by suspending metro services and blocking roads. Traders are reportedly facing losses of around Rs 3,000 crore following previous rallies in October.

stories.title: Zendaya expands Hollywood Hills estate with another $2M home
stories.summary: Zendaya began her real estate journey with a Mediterranean-style home purchased at age 20 in San Fernando Valley. She later acquired a ranch-style estate in Encino and a luxury condo in Brooklyn Heights. Recently, Zendaya bought a mid-century modern home in Hollywood Hills, previously owned by Ashley Tisdale. She subsequently purchased a neighboring property, a fixer-upper, signaling her intent to renovate it.

stories.title: AI model uses face photos to estimate biological age, predict survival risk in cancer patients
stories.summary: A new AI model, FAHR-Face, estimates biological age and predicts cancer patient survival risk using facial photos. This model was trained on millions of images and showed an average error of about five years. Alongside this, another model identified high-risk cancer patients based on their appearance, highlighting significant survival differences. While results were promising in the US and Netherlands, further validation is needed in other populations.

Despite the friction, he remains hopeful for a resolution to the ongoing trade conflict.

stories.title: ABBA’s Chiquitita raised over $5 million for UNICEF in 45 years; how the 1979 hit continues to protect children

stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is set to store crude oil in Singapore starting in the second half of 2027. This arrangement aims to enhance energy security in the region amid supply disruptions. Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns will provide storage facilities for Saudi crude oil supplies. The agreement will allow Saudi Aramco to bring supplies closer to key Asian markets.

The planned changes would replace licence fees with state budget allocations, raising concerns about media independence. Critics argue that these measures may expose broadcasters to political pressure and reduce their financial stability. Public media employees announced plans for a strike on November 3, with a larger rally scheduled for November 15.

stories.summary: John Stamos’s luxurious California mansion has experienced substantial price drops since 2025. Initially, this Mediterranean-style estate in Calabasas was priced near $13 million, but after renovations by the current owners, it now stands at about $6.4 million. Stamos originally acquired the property in 1991 for $430,000 and sold it in 2001, illustrating the complexities in marketing highly personalized high-end real estate.

stories.summary: David L Cohen and Rhonda R Cohen have made an impressive commitment of $10.5 million to the Philadelphia Orchestra. Their contribution will establish the Fund for Cultural Diplomacy, enhancing the orchestra's role as a cultural ambassador, alongside launching the Artistic Innovation and Discovery Fund to spotlight underrepresented composers.

The request for information was made under the Right to Information Act. A social activist from Telangana sought details about the software and algorithms used in the process. The Commission stated that no new software was developed for the exercise conducted.

stories.title: Hendrie Ranch Conservation Easement: Florida approves $12.9m deal; wildlife corridor stays working
stories.summary: A 5,610-acre section of Hendrie Ranch will remain undeveloped due to a $12.9 million conservation easement. This agreement, approved by state officials, allows continued agricultural use while protecting the land from development. The ranch supports cattle, hay production, and timber harvesting alongside diverse wildlife habitats. It is part of Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program to safeguard agricultural properties.

stories.title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to government than needed, says Justice Kaul
stories.summary: Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has expressed concerns about how former Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud dealt with the government. He believes Chandrachud was too lenient during the process of judicial appointments, which raises worries about the independence of the judiciary. This could potentially undermine the separation between the courts and the government, according to Kaul.

stories.title: EPFO considers Rs 25,000cr war chest to stabilise interest payouts
stories.summary: Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation is exploring the establishment of a Rs 25,000-crore Interest Stabilisation Reserve. This reserve aims to protect members’ interest payouts from corporate bond defaults and other market fluctuations. A report suggested that the fund should be built via surplus ETF gains and will invest in government securities. Historical performance indicates that this reserve can effectively manage interest rate stability.

stories.title: Delaware couple wins HOA garage dispute as court orders removal of property violation notice
stories.summary: John and Sandra Mitchell have won a court case against their homeowners association regarding garage construction plans. They proposed a 24-by-28-foot garage with metal siding, which the board initially rejected. The court ruled that the association overstepped its authority by denying the materials without clear restrictions. The violation notice against their property was ordered to be removed from public records.

stories.title: BJP calls protest over Kharge’s ‘baap’ remark
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father sparked widespread outrage among BJP members. Following the incident, the BJP announced nationwide protests against Kharge's remarks, labeling them indecent and offensive. Union home minister Amit Shah criticized Congress for personal attacks and blamed it on their electoral disappointments. Kharge also condemned the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, describing it as a threat to democracy.

stories.title: New York man challenges bank over 2005 mortgage, wins appeal in foreclosure dispute
stories.summary: A New York homeowner who took out a mortgage in 2005 has secured a reversal of a foreclosure ruling that had favoured US Bank National Association. Moses Sukljian challenged the bank's right to enforce the loan after it accused him of missing payments. On Friday, an appeals court overturned the earlier ruling, finding that the bank had failed to provide sufficient proof of its legal standing.

stories.title: Trump gears up for Iran escalation after US polls; Tehran says position unchanged
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has signaled potential military action against Iran following the upcoming midterm elections. The US has increased its military presence in the Persian Gulf with additional aircraft and troops. Iran is reportedly preparing for retaliation against US and allied interests in the region. Both Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu may view renewed conflict as a political strategy.

stories.title: Kentucky court halts inquiry into widow's mental capacity after she rejects late husband's will
stories.summary: A Kentucky appeals court ruled that a district court could not investigate Tamara Williams' mental capacity claim. The dispute arose over her choice to reject her late husband Julian D. Williams' will for a statutory share. After her husband's death, Tamara's decision was contested by his stepchildren, who claimed she lacked mental capacity. The appeals court determined that contested cases must be resolved in circuit court rather than district court.

George Harrison donated his album royalties to charity. In 2024, his foundation spent £573,221
stories.summary: George Harrison's Material World Foundation continues to thrive, providing substantial funding to charitable initiatives worldwide. In 2024 alone, the foundation allocated over £573,000 towards public health, education, and emergency relief efforts. Operated independently by a board of trustees including Olivia Harrison, it eschews salaries to focus all resources on its mission. Founded from royalties of Harrison's classic album, Living in the Material World, the foundation's influence endures, promoting lasting change.

stories.title: New York couple pledges $10 million to expand NICU after granddaughter’s birth experience
stories.summary: Donald and Barbara Zucker have pledged a remarkable $10 million to elevate the standard of neonatal intensive care at Good Samaritan University Hospital. This generous commitment will be complemented by donations from the community, amplifying its reach. The initiative aims to upgrade the neonatal unit with cutting-edge technology and supportive amenities, ensuring high-risk newborns and their families receive essential care in a nurturing environment close to home.

stories.title: Kansas appeals court reopens divorce property case after jailed husband missed hearing next door
stories.summary: A Kansas appeals court recently vacated a previous ruling in a divorce property case, asserting that Scott L. Hale was not given a fair chance to participate. Haltingly unable to attend his hearing due to incarceration, Scott's objections to the property division were overlooked by the trial judge. The court's decision sends the matter back to the lower court for a comprehensive reassessment and new hearing.

Texas student builds landscaping business to fund college, wins national agribusiness award

The business has also helped him support his family financially. His efforts earned him the 2026 American Star in Agribusiness award from the National FFA Organization on Friday.

stories.title: 80-ton boulder collapses at park after 104 years, smashing a walkway but injuring no one
stories.summary: In a surprising turn of events on October 18, 2026, an 80-ton granite boulder collapsed at Polar Caves Park in Rumney, New Hampshire, smashing a wooden walkway and its safety rails. Fortunately, this incident resulted in no injuries. The boulder's fall is likely due to weather-related erosion. Park authorities are now assessing the situation and implementing repair plans to allow for a safe return of visitors in spring 2027.

stories.title: Alabama lawyer gave up career to care for parents, but court upheld cancellation of her condo deed
stories.summary: The Alabama Supreme Court has affirmed a lower court's ruling that invalidated a property transfer from parents to their daughter, Holly Schumpert. Despite her dedication in caring for her ailing parents, the court determined the coastal condominium was part of a family trust, rendering the deed null. As a result, laws designed to protect elderly property owners allowed the reversal, leading to Holly having no claim to the estate.

stories.title: Delhi Police file FIR against opposition MPs over alleged trespassing at Jamia during student protest
stories.summary: The Delhi Police has launched an FIR targeting Congress MPs who attended the student protests at Jamia Millia Islamia. The MPs are accused of entering the university without permission amid ongoing demands for reinstating the students' union. Protesters are also calling for a halt to disciplinary measures against students and improved campus facilities, while university officials draft guidelines for upcoming union elections, adding to the complexity of the situation.

Thanks to DNA evidence, he was arrested and convicted of first-degree murder, rape, and burglary. Faith's lifeless body was found in her apartment in September 2012 after a fun night out.

stories.title: After years of abandonment, 48 acres once home to Ohio's SeaWorld and Six Flags parks are set to reopen on October 25
stories.summary: Aurora Park at Geauga Lake will reopen to the public on October 25, focusing on outdoor recreation. This redevelopment includes seating areas, boating access, and restored structures from the amusement park era. Future phases will introduce a public beach, playground, and other recreational facilities as part of the project. The City of Aurora acquired the property in December 2024 to ensure public access.

stories.summary: Dr. Navin C. Shah has committed $525,000 to establish a new infectious disease program at BJ Government Medical College. The initiative aims to enhance research, medical training, and patient care for underserved communities in Pune. Collaborating with Johns Hopkins University, the program will focus on public health challenges like tuberculosis and HIV. Faculty and student exchanges are also planned to foster international cooperation in medicine.

BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
stories.summary: On Sunday, four Pakistani fishermen were intercepted by the Border Security Force in the Kutch district of Gujarat. Suspected of illegally fishing in Indian waters for crabs, they were detained following precise intelligence alerts. The crew members, hailing from Chach Jaan Khan village in Sindh province, are now under investigation as the BSF maintains vigilance over the sensitive border region to thwart unauthorized entries.
